blocks.text: When Nigerian soldiers landed in Liberia in 1990 under the ECOMOG flag, they were not invading a neighbour for oil. They were carrying out a choice made in Abuja: that West African wars would not be left to burn, because the flames cross borders. That choice — Africa first, then the rest of the world — is the centrepiece of Nigerian foreign policy.

blocks.title: Foreign policy
blocks.text: The strategy a sovereign state adopts in its dealings with other states and international organisations, in order to protect and promote its national interest. It covers diplomacy, trade, aid, military action and membership of international bodies.

blocks.markdown:
### Nigeria's objectives

From independence, official statements have clustered around a short list: the **protection of Nigeria's sovereignty, territorial integrity and security**; the **promotion of the national economic interest** (oil markets, investment, debt, trade); the **well-being of Nigerians at home and abroad**; **African unity, decolonisation and the end of racial domination** on the continent; **international peace and a just world order**, including support for the United Nations; and, during the Cold War, **non-alignment** — refusing to become a satellite of either East or West.

Section 19 of the 1999 Constitution (Chapter II) directs foreign policy towards promotion of African unity, international cooperation, respect for international law, and the settlement of disputes by negotiation. Those Chapter II provisions are not justiciable, but they state the official aims examiners expect you to recite.

rows: Geography
Gulf of Guinea coastline; land borders with Benin, Niger, Chad and Cameroon; leadership role in West Africa
Diplomacy
Embassies, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, presidential visits, mediation
Economy
Oil dependence; need for markets, investment and debt relief; capacity to give or withhold aid
Economic instruments
Trade, oil policy, technical aid, loans and the African Technical Aid Corps
Population and military
Largest population in Africa; a relatively large armed force for regional missions
Military instruments
Peacekeeping (UN, AU, ECOMOG), training, arms and the threat of force
Leadership and public opinion
A President's outlook (Murtala's activism; later isolation under Abacha) can shift tone; domestic opinion constrains adventurism
Propaganda and culture
The press, Nollywood, sport, educational scholarships
History
Colonial experience pushes anti-colonial and anti-apartheid stands
International organisation
UN, AU, ECOWAS, OPEC, the Commonwealth
blocks.caption: Determinants (left) are the conditions that shape choices; instruments (right) are the tools used to carry them out

blocks.markdown:
### Africa as the centrepiece (Afrocentrism)

Nigeria has declared since the 1960s that **Africa is the centrepiece** of its foreign policy: African questions take priority over extra-African ones, and Nigeria will spend blood and money on them.

**Decolonisation.** Nigeria supported liberation movements in Angola, Mozambique, Zimbabwe (then Rhodesia) and Namibia, diplomatically and sometimes with funds and training.

**Anti-apartheid.** Nigeria boycotted South African goods, contributed to the Southern African Relief Fund, chaired UN anti-apartheid efforts, and made itself a leading Frontline-adjacent voice until majority rule in 1994.

**Regional peace.** Nigeria led and largely financed **ECOMOG** (the ECOWAS Monitoring Group) in **Liberia** from 1990 and later in **Sierra Leone**. It has contributed troops to UN and AU missions from the Congo to Darfur and Mali.

**Institution-building.** Nigeria was a founding member of the **OAU (1963)** and a principal architect of **ECOWAS (1975)**, and it hosted and funded much of the later **AU** peace and integration agenda.

Afrocentrism has costs: ECOMOG was expensive in lives and naira, and critics argue that domestic poverty was neglected. Examiners still want the principle named, illustrated, and briefly evaluated.

items: **National interest** — the combined security, economic and prestige goals a state pursues; every other objective is a means to this.
**Non-alignment** — a Cold War doctrine of not joining either NATO or the Warsaw Pact camp; Nigeria was a member of the Non-Aligned Movement.
**Afrocentrism / Africa as centrepiece** — the doctrine that African liberation, peace and unity come first in Nigerian diplomacy.
**Technical Aid Corps** — Nigerian professionals sent to other African and Caribbean states as an instrument of soft power and African solidarity.

blocks.title: Classifying ECOMOG as an Afrocentric instrument
blocks.prompt: Show that the ECOMOG intervention in Liberia (from 1990) illustrates Africa-as-centrepiece, and identify the determinant and the instrument at work.

steps.text: Name the principle. Africa as centrepiece means African crises take priority, even when they are not a direct attack on Nigerian territory.
Name the fact. Nigeria provided the bulk of troops, command and finance for ECOMOG in Liberia, and later in Sierra Leone, under an ECOWAS mandate.

Identify the determinant. Geography (a West African neighbour's war produces refugees, arms and instability on Nigeria's doorstep) plus leadership (Ibrahim Babangida's decision to act) and military capacity.
Identify the instrument. This is a military instrument, used in a peacekeeping/peace-enforcement form, backed by diplomacy inside ECOWAS.
Evaluate in one line. The mission fits Afrocentrism, but the human and financial cost is the standard criticism — a balanced essay mentions both.

blocks.answer: ECOMOG in Liberia was Afrocentrism in practice: a military instrument, driven by West African geography and Nigerian leadership, used to stop a neighbour's war rather than to pursue an extra-African quarrel

blocks.title: Objectives, determinants, instruments — keep the three lists apart
blocks.text: Objectives are what Nigeria wants (security, African unity, economic development). Determinants are why it wants those things in that form (geography, oil, leadership, public opinion, history). Instruments are how it pursues them (diplomacy, economic tools, the military, propaganda, international organisations). Mixing the three is the usual way to lose marks on this topic. For Afrocentrism, always attach a named example: anti-apartheid, Zimbabwe, Namibia, ECOMOG.

points: Foreign policy is a state's strategy for dealing with other states and organisations in pursuit of the national interest.
Nigeria's objectives include sovereignty and security, economic development, the welfare of Nigerians, African unity and decolonisation, international peace, and (historically) non-alignment.
Determinants include geography, the oil economy, population and military capacity, leadership, public opinion and colonial history.
Instruments include diplomacy, economic measures, military force and peacekeeping, propaganda and membership of organisations.
Africa as centrepiece (Afrocentrism) has been shown in support for decolonisation, the anti-apartheid struggle, ECOMOG in Liberia and Sierra Leone, and the founding of OAU/ECOWAS.
